claims.claim: Reviewers report that players are completely unable to harm or kill any wildlife or creatures in the game.

citations.review_text:
As a huge fan of the original this game is a disappointment so far, even giving it grace for being early access. It's definitely a huge improvement graphics-wise and base building is much smoother and more customizable, but the rest feels like a downgrade. I don't mind that the game is incomplete/missing multiple biomes, but there are some design problems I can't look past that take me out of the game. The biggest is the wildlife.

There are tons of arguments online about the fact you can't harm the wildlife in any way, even inadvertently. I understand the design philosophy behind this and I agree Subnautica shouldn't be about combat, but in the original you had your survival knife and could kill things by ramming them. This time they are all literally invincible, even if you ram them at full speed. Not only are the immune from player-caused harm, they also can't kill each other- you'll see predators take down prey only for the prey to get back up and continue swimming soon after.

It also means there are no ways to secure your base from some really annoying predators other than some basic repellant and decoy options. Again, I get the design philosophy, but it makes no sense in the game world. The implementation is ham-fisted and stupid, there was nothing wrong with the approach in the original game. In the original I felt bad if I hit a creature with my vehicle, now it doesn't matter because it is obvious at all times that these are unkillable, unharmable video game objects.

Beyond that I also don't think there's as much variety to the species and they don't have many (or any) environmental interactions. They just swim around in their pre-defined patterns and don't do anything else. Remember sea-monkeys in the original? They'd tease and taunt you, even steal things which you could then retrieve with other goodies at their den. Or the sharkish things (I forget the name) who would collect metal scraps. 

With time and maybe mods it will hopefully become a great game…

Not being able to kill anything is dumb policy... i understand it about leviathans, but not even the annoying ass small ones? that's just ridiculous and not even giving a reason frustrating.  Making it look like they just didn't bother to add  the mechanics.  

Also way to  ruin it  with  the barely legal disclaimer you have to sign to play the game at all - something not clear to you prior to purchase. Be very aware of what your signing when you agree to this EULA.

On the one hand, it's more Subnautica, and it's pretty great for how early in development everything is.


On the other, it's on unreal engine, so it runs like total garbage. I don't think I exceeded 60 FPS a single time playing this game, even at low settings. My PC, while on the older side, can still run most fairly beefy games at a stable 60 FPS to this day. Meanwhile, the EULA is... really bad, like, EA levels of bad. To top it all off, for reasons far beyond me, you are completely and totally unable to harm any wildlife in any capacity. Very odd for a survival game, especially the direct sequel to one that already flawlessly perfected the 'coexistence' message they're trying to force here by making fish pointless and tedious to kill, but not impossible. Even worse, the wildlife can't even hurt each other. You know, the big, scary predators that are supposedly dangerous hunters and strict carnivores? Can't even hurt a fly. It's three steps back, directly into a garden rake, three stooges style, and the dumbest part is that I technically lied, there is one way to hurt wildlife; by kidnapping small fish and slugs in large quantities and either cooking them alive, or grinding them up for water. Totally co-existing with the ecosystem there, guys. It's not like there's a plot point about the entire planet's ecosystem being so fragile that even a slight imbalance could cause an entire ecological collapse. Obviously the solution is to make every living creature in the game completely and totally impervious to being slashed by a hatchet or run into by a submarine made of titanium. Totally not immersion destroying and definitely sends a very clear and cohesive message!


As it stands, I really enjoyed my time with this game. However, I must CURRENTLY give it a thumbs down, so that the devs might see these critiques and actually fix them, as all three are beyond egregious. This game is NOT a bad game, far from it, but I can't in good conscience give this a positive review…
Subnauticaa 2 is as good as the oryginal even tho its in early access, I had fun playing it, The only problem I have with it is the fact that you can't kill any creatures in it

We hyped ourselves up for getting a weapon. Kept saying we will eventually unlock it (to defend ourselves). 7 hours later no weapon found out we cant fight back against any enemies, all you can do is run... "So scary" running away from every enemy you see, and hiding in your vehicle that you can out run or fix when being attacked. Also a fetch quest sim, could have more potential, but the Devs have PETA values

Decent enough survival/basebuilder game, however it's got a glaring issue in it that makes it a chore to play.

There's no way to defend yourself from any form of threat in the game.

Yeah, so basically, if there's a horde of sharks that want to eat you, you can do nothing but allow them to eat and kill you. Building a base nearby any of the shield-faced fished will cause them to gang up on entrances waiting for you.

I'm not asking for a shotgun or some other schut stick, but ffs at least give me a deterrent of SOME kind. Heck, I'd take the freakin' Shark-B-Gone from Adam West's Batman at this point.

Anyways, if you REALLY liked the first game, then get this early access. Otherwise, save your money, time, and sanity and wait for the developers to get off their high horse and fix their game.

Barely scratched the surface.
Only 10hrs in solo and 4hrs in multiplayer. I am thoroughly enjoying the game, environment is pleasant to look at, filled with surreal peaceful scenery with occasional angry ocean monsters to ruin your day. Free roam and missions all provide valuable upgrades which make your journey both more versatile and fun. 

Just need to make the sea monsters able to be attackable & provide benefit from harvesting.

claims.claim: Reviewers note that the game features cooperative multiplayer gameplay.

citations.review_text: I can already tell that Subnautica 2 will be the best subnautica game to date even in its incomplete state.  Base building has been smoothed out and become way more customizable. The sleek graphics are breath taking.  The sound design and voice acting is solid. Believe it or not...best soundtrack.  The story is fantastic, maybe shaping up to be better than the first game?  I love the world building.  Biomes are beautiful and fun to explore. Creature design is really good as well, but still a bit sparse in variety at the moment.  Of course, there's the multiplayer which I haven't gotten to play yet.  I feel so lucky to be able to experience this universe again!

Subnautica 2 is very easy to recommend as it is more of the same great gameplay that made the first game such a hit! Even if you have not played the first game this is worth picking up and playing. Unravel the mystery of the planet!  Gameplay mostly consists of survival, crafting + building and exploration.

The biggest addition here is the co-op feature, playing this game with someone else is brilliant and it really adds to the experience. I am playing with a friend who is on Xbox and we've had no issues joining sessions and playing together.

The game is running very well and so far, I have not encountered any bugs or issues at all and it is in Early Access. Performance is fine and the game in its current state is perfectly playable and a really great experience!

Looking forward to playing more, and I can't wait to see how Subnautica 2 develops further!
Recommended!
Scary but once you have enough friends is so fun! (Everything you see is so pretty)
Its only an Alpha and I already dropped 14 hours. Cant wait to play this with the bro's.

10/10 Love this game! All the same eerie and careful feeling I loved from the original...but I can drag my friends along for the ride!

I love the base building, and the new exploration. The adaptations took a second to get used to, but it just adds more to the game. And the leviathan? Chills! I absolutely recommend this game to anyone who loved the first Subnautica, whether you are wanting to play solo or you also want to bring your friends along!
Its a really good game for playing with friends and family and i do recommend doing so if you get the game
If you liked the first game this one is right up your alley, even though it isn't done just having multiplayer already makes it a huge upgrade.
even though i havent played much its great i never thought that a subnautica game would  have multiplayer

The game is in early access (which means bugs) and looks stunning, the graphics are incredible, the building is a huge step up from the first game and the leviathens aren't all just long worms unlike the first game (the reaper is still an amazing iconic design tho) plus they have better AI. The story is peak and the biomes are unique and cool, they add new mechanics and they are incredible too! My only complaints are ones that are only there because of early access and they will be fixed.

Even after only a few hours, I'm hooked. The world is beautiful, the underwater environments are immersive, and exploring every new biome keeps pulling me in. The story feels more engaging, and the improved base building and quality-of-life changes make the experience smoother without losing that feeling of isolation and discovery.

If you enjoyed the first game, this is an easy recommendation. It's familiar enough to feel like home but different enough to stay exciting. I can't wait to see what else the ocean has in store.

Highly recommended!

ive been a big fan of the series but really the game is not there yet.

Resources scanner is a mess. the tags sometimes bring you to the exact location of the material, some other times close to it, but more often you get to an empty area. (probably the game doesn't track resources depletion) .

Creatures interactions are a mess: predators are unstoppable and will mess with your tadpole and deal massive damage without you being able to defend yourself. no weapons or going full speed against these creatures can help you get rid of them. You get attacked by any lifeform, you have got to retreat. It is very frustrating.

claims.claim: Reviewers describe performance issues, including low frame rates and stuttering, related to Unreal Engine 5.

citations.review_text: Good experience for now from start to the hard end of the current story (ver. 1.1). Needs more more recent hardware than previous games due to the Unreal Engine 5 demand. Will expect more in future updates.

UE5 Slop. Review is based on performance, 
---------Release---------
The game is horribly optimised runs at 60to80 fps on a mixture of high to medium settings with TSR at 75 percent Render scale with and output res of 1440p, The lack of FSR is stupid, the only upscalers they have are DLSS 4.5 and horrible TSR, the choice of using UE5 and not adding support for XESS and FSR is horribly short sighted, this leaves the game looking blurry smeared mess with all graphical improvements over BZ ruined with TSR looking like the equivalent of smearing vasoline on my monitor. Along with all the pains of using UE5 subnautica 2 suffers from traversal sutter and frame time issues.

---------Update 1.1---------
Performance has improved, Ultra settings hovers on the 60fps mark with TSR on 75% scale (1715x965) still no Native FSR support, using a mod for FSR 4 pushes performance to the high 70s mid 80s on Quality (1706x960 internal res, output 2560x1440p), performance is still not ideal but this is a further improvement, Native FSR 4.1 support would drasticly improve visual clarity over TSR. The performance still has a way to go.

claims.claim: Reviewers report that base building is hindered by large space requirements for certain pieces, such as ladders and moonpools.

citations.review_text:
Devs beloved,

Firstly, excellent work so far, there is so much I Love about the new content in this installment (extra pieces to help greeble out larger silhouettes, ladders being being able to face all cardinal directions especially, and MULTIPLAYER <333).

However, as it stands, the base building is having the same pitfalls as the last two games generally, except perhaps even worse than before. For a base building game with lots of terrain variation in all three dimensions, the more pretty and desirable base/outpost locales often wind up a bit cramped, and that's good! The puzzle of finding how to use the space available CAN be very engaging and rewarding. However, the fun of this is almost entirely ruined for me by the absolutely GARGANTUAN space requirements that many base pieces require to be placed.

The chiefest example is, yet again, the ladders. I understand that the placement should require space for both the ladder itself, and for the player to stand upon dismounting, and the game is restricted to a grid-based system. Still, there HAS to be a way, guys. I'm having to plan my bases around ladders more than any other much larger piece. My MOON POOL is easier to figure out than how I can place a ladder AND pretend I've at least HEARD of feng shui. In many other grid based survival base builders, I can place a ladder ON a wall, and the ladder's hitbox is only one grid tile, not... nine at a bare minimum and usually an ENTIRE twenty five. I do not want to have to place almost an entire standard sized room just to HAVE a ladder at all.

This isn't even just about the ladders, of course, they're just the best example. Maybe allow some clipping, guys? Just enough to be sure that some of the pieces I place still stick out a bit if they're phased into each other so I can disassemble if I mess up, and I'm happy. So what if we can clip things into each other? If someone is mad about that, they'd be mad that they made a fixable mistake. It's not like it'd reflect bad…

Another incredible entry in this series. I went and refreshed my memory on the original expansions, and I can say 1000% the best map, the coolest creatures, and the most interesting base building so far

After getting as far as possible in Early Access a little bit solo, and a little bit with friends I'm extremely excited to run through this in multiplayer. The Crushing depths have always haunting and beautiful, and something I want to experience together with other people. The QOL updates for multiplayer alone are a great reason to dip into the game, I had a moment riding as a passenger holding onto a vehicle watching stuff zoom by me that was one of the top 3 moments in subnautica ever

The new building mechanics are STELLAR, the base feels customizable at last, the verticality is a bit meh but customizing the rooms is 10/10. Devs beloved,

Firstly, excellent work so far, there is so much I Love about the new content in this installment (extra pieces to help greeble out larger silhouettes, ladders being being able to face all cardinal directions especially, and MULTIPLAYER <333).

However, as it stands, the base building is having the same pitfalls as the last two games generally, except perhaps even worse than before. For a base building game with lots of terrain variation in all three dimensions, the more pretty and desirable base/outpost locales often wind up a bit cramped, and that's good! The puzzle of finding how to use the space available CAN be very engaging and rewarding. However, the fun of this is almost entirely ruined for me by the absolutely GARGANTUAN space requirements that many base pieces require to be placed.

The chiefest example is, yet again, the ladders. I understand that the placement should require space for both the ladder itself, and for the player to stand upon dismounting, and the game is restricted to a grid-based system. Still, there HAS to be a way, guys. I'm having to plan my bases around ladders more than any other much larger piece. My MOON POOL is easier to figure out than how I can place a ladder AND pretend I've at least HEARD of feng shui. In many other grid based survival base builders, I can place a ladder ON a wall, and the ladder's hitbox is only one grid tile, not... nine at a bare minimum and usually an ENTIRE twenty five. I do not want to have to place almost an entire standard sized room just to HAVE a ladder at all.

This isn't even just about the ladders, of course, they're just the best example. Maybe allow some clipping, guys? Just enough to be sure that some of the pieces I place still stick out a bit if they're phased into each other so I can disassemble if I mess up, and I'm happy. So what if we can clip things into each other? If someone is mad about that, they'd be mad that they made a fixable mistake. It's not like it'd reflect bad…

claims.claim: Reviewers note that aggressive predators cannot be harmed or killed with weapons, which limits defensive options.

citations.review_text:
I am aware it is still in development.

This game is beautiful.  But I find it frustrating more often than I find it fun.  Progress is slow, but not in a satisfying way.  It seems to slow you down just for the purpose of making the game longer.  Goals are not clear and not at all in a real life sort of way. 

I really dislike that you cannot harm the predators at all.  I get that not killing the predators is useful for the game mechanics but really... We have super advanced technology but we can't shock or hurt a predator enough to leave us alone for a bit?  So frustrating and so not believable it hurts immersion.  

I know there is a mode to turn off all threats but then there is no exploration need.  I hate the all or nothing option.  I hope they add sliding difficulties like valhiem did.

"If you wanna kill something, go play Sons of the forest" --- That is some crap coming from the devs. Im not even saying I wanna run around and merc all the fish, I just want some self defense, more so than one freaking ability. That is ridiculous. This game has great potential, but the attitude of the devs is inexcusable.

That doesn't even touch the whole Licensing not owning but renting thing.

claims.claim: Reviewers report that aggressive predators are too easy to avoid and lack a genuine threat or fear factor.

citations.review_text:
Subnautica 2 is shaping up to be an absolute banger. 

Pros:
-Much improved graphics
-Great sound design
-Control is fluid and natural, devs have added sprinting
-Changing bio traits makes the gameplay interesting and supports more diverse strategies
-Base building massively improved compared to first game
-Designed for coop

Cons:
-Biomes do not feel very dangerous (predators are easy to outrun/do not do much damage)
-Few leviathan class organisms
-Small map (at time of writing, still early access)

The current build is a great framework for what I hope to be a much richer storyline with deeper exploration. The devs are doing a great job at listening to the community, and I'm looking forward to their end of year update!

Absolutely loved the experience!
Feels like a fitting, beautiful, and refreshing continuation of the series. The early access story line has, in my opinion, a perfect amount of grinding and lore for the time being. My only gripe with the current build is that it lacks the sense of danger the first game had. The predators are really easy to avoid and after encountering them a few times they lose their fear factor.

citations.review_text: fix base building pls. there is a one inch moon pool inside of a small room that I can't get rid of. Please for the love of god fix the deconstructing and base building bugs and you will all be reincarnated into beautiful flowers.

I was optimistic and gave it a real shot but it's clear the devs just arent sure which direction to take this game. they allow very limited feedback from players and seem to think they know what their fans want more than their fans do lol. inconsistent game mechanics coupled with very obscure storyline direction make players unsure if the problems they are having are due to a bug, or alack of information. Even teh build mechanics are glitchy. one minute my tadpole dock works fine, the next, im getting an error that says theres not enough room to dock. did my building shrink or something?  plus, the devs are insistent that its a "no kill" survival game and refuse to let players clear an area of threats for a few minutes, yet they have players snatching some of the cuter, more docile creatures right out of the water column and eating them alive for hydration or food. and your player needs food and water with ridiculous frequency. with no ability to stack items and a high demand for materials, you need ridiculous amounts of storage containers because none hold much of anything.  updates are slow to be released. the list of complaints goes on. it LOOKS cool tho. i'm gonna take this one out of my favorites and let it sit for a few months. Maybe it'll be a little more friendly to play after the devs have worked out their company issues. Disappointing tho. has the foundations of an awesome game. they should take some cues from channel 37. Those guys know how to dev the crap out of a game!

citations.review_text: Really fun to play, whether you play solo or with friends, it is fun either way!

I never expected to see another Subnautica, and, I am pleased to say that this game is a hitter. Love it a lot, also the coop is pretty dope. The new building stuff is incredible, also I hope they somehow make the placement checker for the ladders a bit smaller so we don't need enormous amount of empty space just for a ladder between floors. Even an elevator could be some thing cool to add in the future. I hope this one will have a giant map, tons of new things to do, and also allow a bit more nudging for building. Other as that I have no complains at all. I'm looking forward for more!

Well like the 1st an Below Zero, this one doesnt disappoint. the game has amazing visuals an the lore is just as good as the first 2. gameplay is really good for it being in early release, an not to mention the amount of content in the game has lots to offer. the multiplayer is fun an def has its funny moments. I still prefer playing by myself most of time, yet the game was still enjoyable. now all im waiting for is the future of this amazing game!
